key_drivers.name: Moscow refinery outage confirmed by Reuters industry sources
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported that the Moscow refinery halted crude processing after fires affected both primary crude-distillation units; sources said restoration could take several weeks. The plant processed about 230,000 bpd in 2024.
key_drivers.interpretation: This upgrades the prior event from physical damage with unknown throughput impact to a material refined-product outage, increasing diesel/gasoline and European energy-risk pressure without implying an equal global crude-supply loss.

key_drivers.name: Oil settles lower on diplomacy hopes and partial Saudi recovery
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported November Brent settled at $100.34/bbl on September 21, down 3.4%; expiring October WTI settled at $95.78, down 4.51%. Saudi oil moving through Hormuz averaged 2.9 million bpd over six days versus 0.7 million bpd in August.
key_drivers.interpretation: Saudi adaptation and diplomacy expectations reduce immediate crude-price pressure, but do not normalize Hormuz shipping or eliminate Middle East tail risk.

key_drivers.name: U.S. reiterates Taiwan Strait stability ahead of Trump-Xi summit
key_drivers.observed: The U.S., Japan and South Korea emphasized peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait and resistance to arbitrary export restrictions ahead of the September 24 Trump-Xi summit.
key_drivers.interpretation: This is a policy-signaling watch item rather than a new military or export-control shock.
